newsitem.title: USA: Science information should be shared, U.S. panel says.
newsitem.headline: Science information should be shared, U.S. panel says.

text.p: Scientific research funded by tax dollars should be freely shared and not restricted by intellectual property laws, a National Research Council panel said on Thursday.
Scientists and educators routinely share publicly funded research data in hopes of speeding medical treatment, food production, communication and other areas.

"Fair use" exceptions to copyright laws allows this exchange for teaching or research purposes but some new proposals do not recognise "fair use" and would charge commercial rates for use of these data bases, even when the research was publicly funded.
Similarly, a trend toward privatisation of data distribution now handled by governments could limit the flow of information, the panel said.

"Science is a cumulative process and laws that inhibit the flow of science information by making it unaffordable would force cutbacks in research as well as significantly slow our progress in science and technology," said committee chair Stephen Berry, a University of Chicago chemist.

The panel said the intellectual property directive of the Commission of the European Communities does not give enough exceptions for researchers, and it said it was worried that a revised version of the treaty being drafted by the U.N.-affiliated World Intellectual Property Organisation would have inadequate provisions for access to scientific research.
The experts said they did recognise the need to protect database vendors from people who unscrupulously copy and distribute it but said a balance must be found to protect science as well.
The council is part of the nonprofit National Academy of Sciences, and helps give science and technology advice to Congress.
